title: Raw weight payload
caption: For $N$ uniformly packed parameters at $b$ bits each. For mixed precision, add the payloads of the separate groups. This excludes scales, padding, other metadata and runtime buffers.

symbols.name: Raw weight payload
symbols.meaning: Bytes needed for the weight values before metadata, padding, and runtime buffers.

symbols.name: Parameter count
symbols.meaning: Number of weight values stored at the given precision.

symbols.name: Bit width
symbols.meaning: Bits stored per weight value.

symbols.name: Unit conversion
symbols.meaning: Bits in one byte.

title: Low-rank weight count and break-even
caption: An $m$ by $n$ matrix is replaced by two factors of shapes $m$ by $r$ and $r$ by $n$. For a matrix-vector product the same counts apply to multiply-accumulates, before intermediate traffic and dispatch.

symbols.name: Factored weight count
symbols.meaning: Values across both factor matrices.

symbols.name: Dense weight count
symbols.meaning: Values in the original weight matrix.

symbols.name: Original shape
symbols.meaning: Rows and columns of the original matrix.

symbols.name: Retained rank
symbols.meaning: Count of retained components, also the width of the intermediate between factor operations.

title: Distillation with hard and soft targets
caption: Both teacher and student soft targets use temperature $T$. Multiplying the soft-target term by $T^2$ compensates for the approximate gradient scaling with temperature. Only the student is needed at inference.

symbols.name: Training loss
symbols.meaning: Scalar objective minimized over student parameters.

symbols.name: Soft-target weight
symbols.meaning: Mixer between zero and one for the distillation term. The remaining weight goes to the supervised loss.

symbols.name: Temperature
symbols.meaning: Positive divisor on logits before softmax. Values above one soften the probabilities.

symbols.name: Hard label
symbols.meaning: Observed target class, represented as a one-hot target for cross-entropy.

symbols.name: Student probabilities
symbols.meaning: Student outputs at temperature one for the hard-label objective.

symbols.name: Soft teacher targets
symbols.meaning: Teacher probabilities after dividing teacher logits by the distillation temperature.

symbols.name: Soft student outputs
symbols.meaning: Student probabilities using the same distillation temperature.

symbols.name: Cross-entropy
symbols.meaning: Hard-target classification loss using the student's probability for the observed class.

symbols.name: KL divergence
symbols.meaning: Measures how the soft student distribution differs from the soft teacher distribution, in the stated direction.

title: Affine quantization and reconstruction
caption: Use a nonzero-width range containing real zero. The integer zero-point anchors zero. Keeping the number of codes fixed makes a wider calibration range increase the step between represented values.

symbols.name: Calibration bounds
symbols.meaning: Lower and upper real-valued endpoints with upper greater than lower.

symbols.name: Code limits
symbols.meaning: Smallest and largest integer codes in the chosen signed or unsigned representation.

symbols.name: Scale
symbols.meaning: Spacing between adjacent represented values in real-value units per code.

symbols.name: Zero-point
symbols.meaning: Integer code used to represent real zero exactly.

symbols.name: Original value
symbols.meaning: Real-valued input before quantization.

symbols.name: Quantized code
symbols.meaning: Integer obtained by rounding, adding the zero-point, and saturating to the code range.

symbols.name: Reconstructed value
symbols.meaning: Real value associated with the stored code.

symbols.name: Rounding
symbols.meaning: Map a real number to its nearest integer under the runtime's tie rule.

symbols.name: Saturation
symbols.meaning: Clamp a code to the allowed endpoints.

title: Bandwidth lower bound for decode
caption: Apply at a fixed batch size and context length for traffic that crosses the same memory interface. Quantizing weights leaves the KV-cache term intact unless it is changed separately.

symbols.name: Token latency
symbols.meaning: Time per decoded token at the stated workload, in seconds.

symbols.name: Weight traffic
symbols.meaning: Weight bytes moved through the selected interface per token. Include quantization metadata in a physical measurement.

symbols.name: KV-cache traffic
symbols.meaning: Key/value cache bytes moved through the same interface per token.

symbols.name: Available bandwidth
symbols.meaning: Bytes per second at that memory interface, using an upper bound for a theoretical latency floor.

title: Traffic of a fused equal-size chain
caption: Counts activation reads and writes for $k$ stages with input and output of size $A$ at every stage, assuming every separate stage spills its output to the interface and fusion can keep intermediates on-chip. Weight reads are counted separately.

symbols.name: Separate-kernel traffic
symbols.meaning: Bytes read and written when every stage materializes output to the memory interface.

symbols.name: Fused-kernel traffic
symbols.meaning: Bytes read and written when the chain keeps every intermediate on-chip.

symbols.name: Stage count
symbols.meaning: Number of operators that each read one input and write one output.

symbols.name: Activation tensor size
symbols.meaning: Identical input and output size for each stage, measured in bytes.

symbols.name: Read plus write
symbols.meaning: Counts one input read and one output write per materialized boundary.

title: Amdahl’s law for an accelerated model stage
caption: This serial-stage model assumes the other work stays fixed. The model share is measured on the original request boundary. Overlapped pipelines require tracing the actual critical path.

symbols.name: End-to-end speedup
symbols.meaning: Baseline request time divided by optimized request time.

symbols.name: Baseline model fraction
symbols.meaning: Fraction of baseline request latency spent in the accelerated stage.

symbols.name: Other work fraction
symbols.meaning: Fraction of baseline request latency unaffected by the stage speedup.

symbols.name: Model-stage speedup
symbols.meaning: Old stage duration divided by new stage duration.

title: Sparse storage break-even with metadata
caption: Each retained value has its own index. Fixed overhead is charged once. The inequality is about storage. Sparse-kernel latency needs a separate experiment.

symbols.name: Dense value count
symbols.meaning: Original number of matrix entries, including zeros.

symbols.name: Sparsity
symbols.meaning: Fraction of original entries stored implicitly as zero.

symbols.name: Value width
symbols.meaning: Bytes used for each stored weight, at the same precision on both sides.

symbols.name: Index width
symbols.meaning: Bytes of position metadata for each retained weight in the chosen format.

symbols.name: Fixed metadata
symbols.meaning: Other bytes needed by the sparse encoding, such as row pointers. These do not scale with the number of retained entries in this model.

symbols.name: Retained density
symbols.meaning: Fraction of the original entries kept as explicit values.
